name: Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting (Katsumata et al.)
definition: An explicit deformation method using Fourier series to fit changes in Gaussian position (inspired by periodic motion) and linear functions to approximate rotation. Other attributes remain unchanged.
summary: Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting models dynamic scenes by parameterizing position and orientation as explicit time-dependent functions, distinguishing itself from implicit deformation networks.
